title: Realistic Counterfactual Explanations via Denial Constraints

problem.claim: Counterfactual explanations are intended to identify feature perturbations that change a classification label while remaining small and useful for explaining predictions.

gap.claim: Methods that optimize proximity and diversity may produce counterfactual explanations that do not correspond to realistic instances, limiting practical applicability and usefulness.

contributions.claim: The approach represents counterfactual realism using logical denial constraints defined with respect to a dataset of examples.
The approach combines counterfactual-generation solutions with adapted data-cleaning ideas to transform counterfactuals into realistic ones.
The paper develops dedicated optimizations to speed up the search for counterfactuals.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments across four datasets report that the solutions achieve realism with a relatively minor compromise in distance and diversity.
Experiments report that the dedicated search optimizations are highly effective.

narrative_sequence.summary: Counterfactuals explain classifications by making small instance perturbations that change the predicted label.
Existing methods emphasize proximity to the original instance and diversity among counterfactuals.
These objectives can produce counterfactuals that are unrealistic and less useful in practice.
The paper models realism with denial constraints and adapts data-cleaning techniques to transform generated counterfactuals.
Experiments on four datasets report favorable realism-distance-diversity tradeoffs and effective search optimizations.

source_observation.claim: Realism can be operationalized through logical constraints learned or specified with respect to a dataset of examples.

interpretation.claim: Explanation quality may require validity criteria beyond proximity to the original instance and diversity among explanations.

application.claim: Use domain or dataset-backed constraints to filter or repair generated explanations before presenting them to users.

exception.claim: Constraint-based realism may involve a tradeoff with distance and diversity.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the counterfactual-generation algorithms or data-cleaning adaptations.
The four datasets, denial constraints, baselines, and quantitative results are not identified.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
